title: Egress connection timeline - scratchbook
content:
Goal:
Quick reproduction notes + timeline for intermittent egress TLS resets observed from private deployment clusters in eu-west-1. This is my lab scratchbook: commands I ran, raw snippets I saved, and immediate hypotheses. Not polished — just breadcrumbs for follow-up and for whoever picks this up oncall.

Summary of observable symptom:
- Intermittent TLS connection closures (RST/early EOF) from service instances talking to external API endpoints (api.partner.example.com) around 08:30-09:40 UTC on repeated days.
- Failures spike during rolling backups and when cross-account peering sync tasks run.
- Requests sometimes succeed after a retry ~200ms later.

Quick hypothesis (top of mind):
1) Short asymmetric routing window where return path goes via a different NAT host without established conntrack entry -> RST on return.
2) DNS TTL churn + client caching combined with ephemeral backend IPs during maintenance -> some clients talk to decommissioned host -> TCP RST.
3) TLS SNI mismatch / ALPN negotiation edge-case with HTTP/2 -> server resets early for certain IPs (less likely but observed in one capture).

Timeline / commands tried (raw):
2024-10-12 09:02 - basic reproducer from a failing pod - curl -v --resolve "api.partner.example.com:443:34.210.12.99" https://api.partner.example.com/health --http2 --max-time 6
  * Connected to 34.210.12.99 (34.210.12.99) port 443 (#0)
  * ALPN, offering h2
  * TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
  * server did not present certificate chain
  curl: (56) recv failure: Connection reset by peer

Note: same curl to other resolved IPs worked.

2024-10-12 09:05 - packet capture (tcpdump) on node during repro window:
- tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/pcap-0910.pcap host 34.210.12.99 and port 443
- Observed TCP handshake complete, TLS ClientHello, then single ACK + RST from remote ~120ms after client finished ClientHello. No TLS ServerHello.
- export of hex snippet saved as tls-clienthello-hex.txt (raw bytes).

2024-10-12 09:10 - ss / conntrack checks - ss -tmi sport = :443 dst 10.0.5.32 - conntrack -L | grep 34.210.12.99
  * conntrack: entry present for most successful flows, but for failing ones I saw only SYN_RECV or missing entry (race).

2024-10-12 09:15 - traceroutes - traceroute -T -p 443 34.210.12.99  (on host)
  * pathA: node -> transit-gw-a -> nat-1 -> internet
  * pathB (for other IP): node -> transit-gw-b -> nat-2 -> internet
  Observation: two distinct egress NATs; NAT-1 shows higher retransmits in sar logs for kernel tcp.

2024-10-12 09:22 - DNS experiments - dig +noall +answer api.partner.example.com @8.8.8.8
- dig +short api.partner.example.com @our-internal-resolver | sort -u
  * TTLs vary (10s -> 300s), partner rotates A records quickly during maintenance windows.
  * Added curl with --dns-servers pointing to different resolvers: behavior changed (some resolvers return older A).

2024-10-12 09:35 - openssl s_client deeper probe - openssl s_client -connect 34.210.12.99:443 -servername api.partner.example.com -alpn h2 -tlsextdebug -msg -debug
  * Received TLS alert: 40 (handshake_failure) in one attempt. In another attempt remote closed socket mid-handshake with no alert.

2024-10-12 09:40 - strace attached to failing curl process in container - strace -f -s 200 -o /tmp/strace-curl.txt curl ...
  * last syscall: write(5, "<ClientHello bytes>", 1420) = 1420
  * next: recvmsg(5, ...) = -1 ECONNRESET (Connection reset by peer)

Other checks I ran:
- ip route show table all (looked for route flaps) — no obvious route changes at kernel table level at repro time.
- dmesg /var/log/kern.log — found occasional "nf_conntrack: table full" warnings on one NAT host about once/day (capacity tuning candidate).
- nft list ruleset / iptables-save — validated no recent DROP rules matching destination IPs.
- eBPF tcp drop probe with bpftrace on node to count tcp_rst events per dest IP over time. Result: spike aligned with repro window.

Correlation with infra events:
- 08:50 UTC — cross-account peering route propagation job (automated) started (internal ticket). Route updates coincide with spike windows.
- 09:00 UTC — partner rotated A records for api.partner.example.com (their status page).

Unique observations (why this feels like asymmetric/race case):
- Packet captures show ClientHello leaving node but no ServerHello and then RST from remote; conntrack missing on return path suggests maybe return hits different NAT without state.
- Some clients had short-lived ephemeral source ports >60000; others re-use. When source port was re-used we saw fewer failures (consistent connection reuse helps).
- On NAT host with conntrack warnings, increasing nf_conntrack_max reduced repro frequency in lab (temporary test).

Immediate mitigations tried (and results):
- Force HTTP/1.1 (curl --http1.1) — no effect in failing case (still RST).
- Disable HTTP/2/ALPN in client library — sometimes changes timing but not root cause.
- Pin DNS to single resolver with long ttl (workaround) — reduced incidents for short-term tests. Not a long-term fix.
- Added temporary iptables rule on NAT host to accept RELATED/ESTABLISHED more permissively — seemed to reduce failures while deployed (suggests conntrack interference).

Commands I want to preserve for next investigator (copy/paste):
- tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/pcap-$(date +%H%M).pcap host <dst_ip> and port 443 and host <pod_ip>
- ss -tmi | grep <pod_ip> || true
- sudo conntrack -L | egrep "<pod_ip>|<dst_ip>" || true
- sudo bpftrace -e 'kprobe:tcp_v4_send_reset { @[comm,inet_ntop(args->daddr)]++ }'  (to catch who is sending resets locally)
- sudo netstat -s | egrep "retransmit|reset" -A3
- openssl s_client -connect <dst_ip>:443 -servername api.partner.example.com -alpn h2 -tlsextdebug -msg -debug

Hypotheses (detailed):
- H1 NAT conntrack exhaustion on transient NAT host: conntrack table full or eviction leads to symmetric path issues; remote RSTs when return hits a different NAT. Evidence: conntrack warnings in kernel log; iptables ACCEPT tweak helped.
- H2 Route flap causing one-way packet flow for few 100ms windows: route propagation job updates BGP/peering table and transit gateway selects alternate NAT depending on per-packet hashing -> return path mismatch. Evidence: peering job timing correlation; traceroute differences between IPs.
- H3 Partner-side load-balancer misconfiguration: for certain IPs LB drops early (handshake failure) when SNI matches certain hostnames or when backend is draining. Evidence: partner status page, handshake_failure alerts in one openssl run.
- H4 DNS TTL churn: clients have stale A records pointing to old/warm instances that are decommissioned -> immediate RST. Evidence: varied TTLs, replication delay across resolvers.

Next steps checklist (what I plan / recommend to do next):
- Reproduce in controlled lab: spin two NAT hosts and intentionally evict conntrack entries to see RST behavior end-to-end. (I have small terraform module started under /tmp/tf-egress-repro).
- Coordinate with network infra to watch conntrack usage on NAT-1 and NAT-2 during the next peering job: enable extended conntrack logging.
- Ask partner to provide proxy log lines for failing timestamps (they may show backend drain or TLS policy). Linked ticket above.
- Add temporary connection affinity on transit gateway if possible (force source-path symmetry) while we verify.
- Implement small client-side retry/backoff with jitter for TLS handshake failures to mitigate impact quickly.

Loose notes for whoever picks this up:
- If you see many ECONNRESET with no ServerHello in pcaps, check conntrack and nat host kernel logs first.
- Avoid rolling changes to many NAT hosts at once; we saw correlation with backup tasks that touched routes.
- Check nftables 'ct helper' settings if using FTP or unusual protocols; not applicable here but worth sanity check.

Attachments mentioned/created during debug (local):
- /tmp/pcap-0910.pcap (raw capture)
- /tmp/strace-curl.txt
- tls-clienthello-hex.txt
- /var/log/messages: nf_conntrack warnings (excerpt saved to conntrack-warn-1012.txt)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Exact internal hashing for transit gateway -> NAT mapping (per-packet or per-flow) unknown. Need infra to confirm.
- Were there any kernel upgrades or sysctl changes around 09:00 on NAT-1? (need SRE logs).
- Is partner LB performing any active RSTs for malformed ClientHello patterns (SNI or extension mismatch)?

If you take this on: start by grabbing the PCAP and filter for TLS ClientHello sequences and correlate timestamps with NAT host conntrack dumps and transit-gw route-change logs. If you want me to hand off, ping me and I will drop the Terraform repro module link and the small helper scripts I used.

End of scratchbook.
notes: Informal; intended as a personal scratchpad. Save any definitive runbooks elsewhere (product or SRE playbooks).
